name: Vex'ara, the Sultress of Chains
description: Vex'ara is a deity of bondage, submission, and exquisite torment. She delights in the aesthetics of restraint and the surrender of free will. Her followers are often bound in elaborate, beautiful shackles, and her temples are filled with intricate cages and terrifying instruments of torture. She demands sacrifices of personal freedom or voluntary suffering, such as choosing to lock on oneself one of the implements of bondage or torture usually found at her altars. In return, she grants a boon of easily removing the next piece of bondage locked on oneself.

name: Morbis, the Flesh-Shaper
description: Morbis is a god of transformative flesh, carnal mutation, and grotesque beauty. He finds ecstasy in the reshaping of living forms, twisting bodies into new, often lewd or monstrous, configurations. His altars are adorned with pulsating organs and shifting biomatter. He demands sacrifices of bodily integrity, a limb, or an organ, offered willingly or taken by force. His boons include the power to alter one's own or others' physical forms, for a short duration after making the offering, and only within the altar's bounds.

name: Xylos, the Parasitic Bloom
description: Xylos is a god of parasitic symbiosis, transformative fertility, and grotesque fecundity. He views parasites not as invaders, but as sacred catalysts for divine change. His altars are living masses of pulsating tendrils and swollen, seed-filled pods. He demands the sacrifice of a parasite currently infesting the supplicant's body, which his power will painlessly extract and consume. In exchange, he grants the 'boon' of hyperfertility, causing the supplicant's sexual organs to swell to immense, immobile proportions. Breasts become titanic milk-fonts, hips widen into birthing arches, and genitals transform into perpetually receptive, dripping gateways. Movement becomes a laborious crawl, the body a monument to fertile excess.

name: Amaranthia, the Progenitrix of Monsters
description: Amaranthia is the primordial goddess of monster girls, the wellspring from which all their varied and beautiful lineages flow. Her altar is a serene pool of iridescent liquid, surrounded by carvings of lamias, harpies, slime girls, and countless other forms. The altar is innert to those without monster girl blood. If a true monster girl prays here, she awakens the deep power of her lineage, gaining great strength, potent innate magic, or a majestic transformation befitting her kind. If a non-monster girl disturbs the altar, through touch, theft, or mockery, it places upon them an unbreakable geas of absolute submission. They become compelled to seek out the next monster girl they encounter and offer themselves as her eternal, devoted slave, their will forever bound to her whims.

name: Valyra, the Pathfinder's Patron
description: Valyra is the benevolent goddess of adventurers, wanderers, and those who brave the unknown. She offers sanctuary and aid to those who carry the burdens of the dungeon. Her altar is simple and sturdy, often adorned with worn maps, well-used gear, and tokens left by grateful travelers. She will remove one affliction from the supplicant: a cursed item, a locked piece of bondage, a parasitic infestation, a magical brand, etc. If the supplicant carries no such burdens, she may instead grant a boon in the form of a powerful weapon suited to their style, or a potent, reliable ability to aid their survival. In exchange, the supplicant must always wear a simple, unadorned metal tag around their neck, bearing her sigil. This tag is a symbol of her favor and a ward against despair. If it is ever removed, lost, or taken by force, her favor is withdrawn. From that moment on, every monster the adventurer faces will be subtly empowered, stronger, faster, and more relentless, making future combat nearly impossible to win until the tag is recovered.
